back: Lasting for a very short time; transitory. "The ephemeral beauty of cherry blossoms lasts only a week."
A person who flatters someone influential in hopes of personal gain. (Adj: sycophantic)
Having a ready insight into things; shrewd. "A perspicacious investor spots trends before the crowd."
Noisy and difficult to control; unruly. "The obstreperous crowd drowned out the speaker."
Tending to talk a great deal; talkative. Antonym: laconic.
Sweet or musical; pleasant to hear. "Her mellifluous voice could calm any room."
Deceitful and untrustworthy; guilty of betrayal. (Noun: perfidy)
Stubbornly resistant to authority or control. "The recalcitrant student refused every instruction."
To make unclear or unintelligible; to confuse deliberately. "The report was designed to obfuscate rather than inform."
Optimistic, especially in a difficult situation. "She remained sanguine despite the setbacks." (Not to be confused with sanguinary = bloody.)
Eager or quick to argue or fight; aggressively defiant. "The truculent defendant glared at the jury."
Using very few words. From Laconia (Sparta), whose citizens were famed for terse speech. Antonym: loquacious.
Clear, logical, and convincing. "She made a cogent argument that swayed the entire committee."
To use ambiguous language to conceal the truth or avoid commitment. "The politician equivocated when asked a direct question."
Having a habit or interest long-established and unlikely to change. "An inveterate traveller, she had visited over 80 countries."
